answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance comes from bonded stakes that are slashable upon detection. Across the open tundra of the network, every account must lock capital proportional to its influence. Coordinated fake identities show juniper-like rapid proliferation in activity graphs; once confirmed by peer attestations the stake is destroyed as thoroughly as soft shale, so the attacker loses real money for each forged node and the total cost quickly surpasses any gain from manipulating rankings or rewards.
